author: Mateusz Pusz
description:
The fourth part of a series on C++ fundamentals covers where reinterpret_cast is actually well-defined. It walks through reading an object’s bytes, aliasing through a signed/unsigned pair, moving between a struct and its first member, and round-tripping a pointer through std::uintptr_t.

Type punning done right

by Mateusz Pusz

From the article:

You may always access the object representation of any object through a pointer to char, unsigned char, or std::byte. The object representation is the sequence of sizeof(T) bytes that make up the object, and reading it as bytes is exactly what serialization, hashing, and hex dumps do.
